title: Chapter 2: Claude Agent SDK Deep Dive

questions.question: What are the three core primitives of the Claude Agent SDK?
questions.explanation: The three core primitives of the Claude Agent SDK are: Agent (defines the agent), Tool (a callable function), and Runner (executes the agent loop). These three primitives are all you need to build a production agent.

questions.question: What is the correct order of the Claude agent execution loop?

options.C: Receive -> Build context -> Send to Claude -> Process response -> (loop if tool call)

questions.explanation: The agent loop is: (1) Receive user message, (2) Build context with system prompt + history + tool schemas, (3) Send to Claude API, (4) If Claude returns TOOL_USE — execute it and loop back; if TEXT — return the final response.

questions.question: What type of data should a Tool handler return?

options.A: A formatted prose paragraph for Claude to display directly
options.B: A JSON-serialisable dict — Claude will compose the prose
options.C: Raw HTML for the frontend to render
options.D: A Python object (Claude can introspect it)

questions.explanation: Tools should return JSON-serialisable dicts (structured data). Claude receives this data and composes the prose response. If a tool returns pre-written prose, Claude loses the flexibility to tailor the response to context.

questions.question: What is 'episodic memory' in an AI agent context?

options.A: The model's training data from past internet text
options.B: The current conversation stored in the context window
options.C: Summaries of past agent runs, retrieved to give continuity across sessions
options.D: A Redis cache of API responses

questions.explanation: Episodic memory stores summaries of past agent runs externally. At the start of a new run, relevant past episodes are retrieved and injected into the system prompt, allowing the agent to say 'Last time we discussed X...' across separate sessions.

questions.question: Why should you always set a max_turns limit on an agent?

options.A: Because Claude cannot handle more than 20 tool calls by design
options.B: To prevent runaway agent loops that could generate unexpected costs
options.C: Because PostgreSQL connections time out after 20 queries
options.D: Because Cloudflare R2 has a 20-read daily limit on free tier

questions.explanation: Without a max_turns limit, a poorly-designed agent can loop indefinitely — making hundreds of LLM API calls and accumulating large unexpected costs before you notice. Always set max_turns=20 (or appropriate limit) as a safety measure.
